laudable

LAW-duh-bul · adjective

Hear It

What It Means

Laudable is deserving praise or admiration.

Though the fundraiser only collected a fraction of its ambitious goal, organizers called the community's laudable turnout on a rainy Tuesday night a real success in itself.

Example

Critics agreed that the freshman senator's laudable attempt to reform the outdated voting system, even though it ultimately failed in committee, showed real political courage.

Laudable praises the effort or intention behind an action -- something can be laudable even if it doesn't fully succeed.

Compare the words

Synonyms · words with a similar meaning

praiseworthy: Praiseworthy is the everyday, all-purpose word for anything that deserves praise, from a good deed to a good grade. Laudable is its more formal cousin, and it usually praises the effort or intention behind an action, even when the result fell short.

commendable: Commendable describes conduct worth singling out for official or public praise -- the word a principal or a review board reaches for. Laudable is close in strength, but it centers on how worthy the attempt itself was, so an effort can stay laudable even after it fails.

What it isn’t · antonyms and near-opposites

deplorable: deserving strong disapproval

disgraceful: shockingly unacceptable; shameful

Where it sits · how much praise it earns

decent → laudable → heroic

decent vs. laudable: Decent just means acceptable or fine -- it doesn't necessarily earn any special admiration the way laudable does.

heroic vs. laudable: Heroic goes even further than laudable, describing an act of extraordinary courage or self-sacrifice.

Build the Word

The pieces

root — laud-: to praise (Latin laudare)

suffix — -able: worthy of (Latin -abilis)

Put it together: Laudable comes from Latin laudare ('to praise') -- the same root behind applaud, literally 'to praise toward' someone, which began as clapping the hands at a performance. A laudable act is, at root, one worth praising.

Use the root in a new word: applaud: Critics who lauded the film in May had gone quiet by August.

Word Choice

Laudable is a formal way to praise an effort or intention -- it works even when the outcome fell short, since it's really commenting on how worthy the attempt itself was.
